page.layout: One printed page, one text column with figures set into it. Running head at the top, page number 77 at the top right. Text runs top to bottom. Three triangle figures sit at left in the column, with the "Exempli causa" caption beside the first. A row of symbols stands between two paragraphs. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: positus est & limitis nomen sibi adoptauit, monstrari
solet, non vero ipse lapis siue limes (alioquin
enim, si ipse lapis agri terminus esset, si lapidem istum tollerem
& in vicini agrum deferrem, tunc simul terminum mei
agri in vicino agro ponerem, & sic facile agrum meum
dilatarem, & vicinum agrum facerem meum) qui tan-
tum loci istius ac termini siue interstitii ac distinctionis
inter vtrosque agros signum est. Caeterum alias An-
gulus definiri solet, quod nihil aliud sit, quam con-
tactus siue concursus duarum plurium-ue linearum: aut
spacium quod proxime adiacet lineis inter se concurrentibus, vt [illegible, ~8 letters]
Theoremata generalia de Angulo sunt ista:
1. Duae lineae quae suo contactu angulu consti-
tuunt, vocantur in Geometria crura angulorum.
Exempli causa: ex concursu duarum
linearum b. a. & c. a. oritur angulus a.
idcirco vocantur istae duae lineae Crura
anguli a:
2. Anguli quorum Crura sunt
aequalia, ipsi sunt inter se aequales.
Hoc Theor: non aliter demonstratur, quam per principium ἐφαρμόσεως, id est, applicationis
linearum & angulorum ad se invicem. Et sane cum angulus nihil sit a-
liud quam concursus duarum
linearum, & cum Crura angu-
li nihil aliud sint quam lineae
duae angulum constituentes,
sequitur necessario angulos
fore aequales, quando crura
sunt aequalia. E. g. sint duae lineae nec[?]

page.notes: The row of symbols after "vt" is printed in a decorative, non-Latin or unreadable shape and is not read. The three triangle figures are drawings with letters a, b, c, d, e, f at their points; they are not transcribed as text. The word ending the last line is partly cut off at the foot of the page and is uncertain. The Greek word ἐφαρμόσεως is copied from a small, worn print and may not be exact. The "& similibus." line is the end of a sentence set beside the symbols.
